ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all founders, directors, shareholders and every UBO against (i) the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, (ii) the Swiss SECO State Secretariat for Economic Affairs and FINMA enforcement lists, (iii) EU consolidated financial sanctions list, (iv) OFAC SDN list and associated lists as red-flag overlay for USD-cleared payment rails (PayPal/Stripe), and (v) PEP definitions under Article 2a AMLA/GwG and FINMA Circular 2019/1; screening must be performed at initiation, on the date of share capital deposit, and at least semi-annually thereafter; adverse hits require enhanced due diligence, senior management sign-off, and, where warranted, suspension of pre-incorporation steps.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: ZEFIX - Zentraler Firmenindex / Swiss Central Business Name Index (https://www.zefix.ch), operated by the Federal Commercial Register, with final scrutiny performed by the Cantonal Commercial Register Office of the registered office (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be formulated in a single official Swiss national language (German, French, Italian or Romansh) without mixing languages unless an exception under Article 950 CO applies; for a Zug-incorporated Aktiengesellschaft, the German-language name form is standard; the suffix Aktiengesellschaft (full form) or AG (abbreviated form) must appear in the company name; names in Latin script derived from foreign words or brand marks are acceptable if distinctly identifiable, non-deceptive and not conflicting with existing protected names; Chinese characters or non-Latin scripts may not be used in the official registered name and may only be referenced in marketing materials without creating any registration-right in the commercial register.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Bankier, Banque, Banca, Versicherung, Assurances, Assicurazione, Anlagefonds, Fonds, Trust, Treuhand, Stiftung (any combination requiring prior FINMA or supervisory approval)

Switzerland, Swiss, Suisse, Svizzera, Helvetia, Schweizer, Eidgenossenschaft, Bund, National (any name with 'Swissness' connotation requires licence under the Swiss Trade Mark Protection Act and the Swissness Act, SR 232.119, based on 75-100% Swiss value creation depending on product category)
Genossenschaft (reserved exclusively for cooperatives), Gemeinde, Kanton, Bundesamt (any official authority designation)

Any token that is misleading, deceptive, contrary to public interest, morality or foreign public order under Article 944 CO and Article 12 HRegV, including names suggesting a state monopoly, mining, military arms, or health-related regulatory attributes absent a corresponding licence
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon commercial-registry refusal of a name, the applicant must, within 30 days of receipt of the written refusal (Verfügung), file a written reconsideration request with the same Cantonal Commercial Register Office of Zug, including corrected alternative names and legal arguments; if the Cantonal Office maintains the refusal, the applicant files an administrative appeal to the Zug Cantonal Court (Kantonsgericht Zug) within 30 days of the reconsideration decision; a further appeal on questions of law may be brought to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court (Bundesgericht) in Lausanne within 30 days pursuant to Article 75 of the Federal Supreme Court Act (BGG); the statutory fee for an appeal is typically CHF 200-500 plus legal fees; during the appeal period, the refused name cannot be used in commerce, and a simultaneous alternative reservation of a back-up name is required to avoid delay of the incorporation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: The physical registered seat of the AG must be in the municipality indicated in the Articles of Association to which the commercial register and tax authorities may validly deliver legal notices; a pure 'virtual office' without any rentable premises is not acceptable for the registered seat; however, a virtual-office or co-working address may be admissible if the company's actual central administration is located in the same municipality or if the service provider offers a conventional physical reception, mail handling and board meeting venue, and the registered office is not established under circumstances indicating evasion of attachments or insolvency law; for an e-commerce FPV racing drone distributor using PayPal/Stripe rails, the cantonal commercial register will likely require at minimum a genuine administrative seat with documented access rights, books and records storage, and a designated person authorised to accept service; a pure mailing-forwarding address without service acceptance is rejected.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced physical on-site inspections: Low-to-Moderate, approximately 8% within the first 24 months of operation; frequency increases to 12-15% if the company applies for VAT/MWST registration, hires employees (AHV/AVS inspection), or if commercial registry or tax office detects abnormal patterns, mismatches between turnover and registered office infrastructure, or repeated relocations; an auditor-mandated inspection is also triggered under Article 958c CO if the statutory audit reveals irregularities; for a low-risk standard retail business without statutory licence requirements, no automatic inspection is scheduled, but Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) and the Cantonal Tax Office of Zug retain the right to conduct unannounced visits.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal fees regulation (Zuger Gebührenverordnung of the Commercial Register Office); CHF 50 standard tariff per name, non-refundable

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office of Zug (Handelsregisteramt Zug)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal fee schedule; CHF 150 per reservation; an extension for a second 180-day period, where granted, is CHF 150 additional

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the formation deed, Articles of Association (Statuten), declaration of capital payment, and board acceptance letter

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal notarial tariff based on share capital, typically 0.2%-0.5% of CHF 100,000 nominal capital with a minimum engagement fee of CHF 1,500; standard quote CHF 2,500 for capital of CHF 100,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial register entry filing fee (federal and cantonal portions) for incorporation of a stock company

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: SR 951.151 (Handelsregister-Gebührenverordnung), Article 3: CHF 800 federal base fee; Canton Zug adds approximately CHF 500; total CHF 1,300

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht/Code des obligations), Art. 620-763 (Aktiengesellschaft); Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV); Federal Act on the Amendment of the Swiss Code of Obligations (Share Capital Reform 2023).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (e.g., Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zürich), supervised by the Federal Department of Justice; centralized name verification through the Swiss Central Business Name Index (ZEFIX).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public Notarial Deed of Incorporation (öffentliche Beurkundung der Statuten) followed by electronic Commercial Register application (Anmeldung) with publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital CHF 100,000; at the time of incorporation at least CHF 50,000 must be paid in cash (or 20% of the nominal value of each subscribed share, if higher); the paid capital must be deposited into a FINMA-supervised blocked bank account (Sperrkonto) and released only upon Commercial Register registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Contribution and Blocked Bank Account Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank or PostFinance, acting under FINMA AML supervision (AMLA/GwG); no government filing at this stage.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Founders open a blocked capital account in the name of the future corporation and deposit at least CHF 50,000. The bank issues a written confirmation of paid-up capital (Einzahlungsbestätigung). Funds remain blocked until Commercial Register registration.
required_dossiers: Founders' valid passports or Swiss/EEA identity cards
Source-of-funds declarations and AML questionnaires for each founder
Draft Articles of Association (Statuten)
Capital payment schedule indicating CHF 100,000 nominal split
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank issues an AML query, provide supplementary source-of-funds documentation or select an alternative FINMA-licensed bank; the deposit structure remains unaffected until regulatory clearance is obtained.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Association and Founder Declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal notary public (Notariat) officially recognized in the canton of the registered office, e.g., Notariat Zürich.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founders present the draft Statuten and capital confirmation before the notary. The notary reads the instrument, authenticates signatures, and issues the public deed, including the declaration that no contributions in kind are made and that the capital has been paid in cash.
required_dossiers: Draft notarial deed of incorporation
Bank confirmation of paid-up capital (Einzahlungsbestätigung)
Share subscription list
Founders' identity documents and permission of residence permits, if non-EU/EFTA
Acceptance declarations of directors and auditor (or waiver of limited audit)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies incomplete corporate data, the deed is corrected by a supplementary declaration and re-signed; any deficient founder signature is re-authenticated before issuance of the final deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register (Handelsregister) Electronic Filing and SHAB Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton (e.g., Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zürich); submission via the EasyGov.swiss portal or directly to the cantonal registry; publication in SHAB.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary or counsel files the public deed and supporting declarations electronically. The registry verifies legal compliance, name uniqueness, and capital confirmation, then issues the registration certificate and arranges SHAB publication.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarial public deed
Bank capital confirmation (Einzahlungsbestätigung)
Directors' and signatories' specimen signature cards
Written consent of the building owner for registered office (domicile authorization)
Declaration under Art. 12 HRegV regarding authorized representatives
Natural persons declaration and residence permits of signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query or provisional refusal, the applicant cures the deficiency within the statutory grace period (usually 10-30 days); an appeal may be filed with the cantonal supervisory authority against a negative final order under HRegV.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Registration Certificate and Post-Incorporation Corporate Actions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office for certificate issuance; Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC) for VAT purposes; Cantonal Tax Office for corporate income tax registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registration, the company obtains the Handelsregisterauszug (extract). The board holds its organizational meeting, opens operational bank accounts, releases the blocked capital, and registers with the VAT registry (MWST/IVA) if taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register extract (Handelsregisterauszug)
Certified copy of the public deed
Directors' identification documents
Expected annual turnover declaration for VAT purposes
Registered office address confirmation and lease agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT or cantonal tax registration is delayed, file a late-registration justification with ESTV or the Cantonal Tax Office; penalties are waived if reasonable cause is demonstrated within 60 days of the extract date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social Insurance, Accident Insurance, and Payroll Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AHV Ausgleichskasse (compensation office) for old-age and survivors insurance; SUVA for compulsory accident insurance; Cantonal Building Insurance (GVA/KGV) for fire and structural coverage.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company registers as an employer with the cantonal AHV compensation office and obtains an employer number. SUVA registration for occupational and non-occupational accident coverage is completed, and a payroll ledger is established for social deductions.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register extract
Directors' and employees' AHV numbers
Payroll structure and salary declarations
Workplace risk assessment plan
Fire safety certificate of the premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the compensation office rejects employer registration due to missing payroll data, supplement the declaration and re-submit; retroactive premiums are adjusted and late payment interest is minimal if corrected without undue delay.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) - Goods Control Office (Güterkontrollstelle) in conjunction with OFCOM (Bakom) for radio-equipment conformity of FPV video transmitters and receivers.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Dual-Use Goods Authorization under the Swiss Goods Control Act (Güterkontrollgesetz/GKG) and Radio-Equipment Type Conformity Declaration (FKV/FACO) for the FPV racing drone product line.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration tier (moderate-volume) per Annex 2 of the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVP/UVPV): sectoral verification for carbon-fiber milling machinery; full EIA report is not required when annual solvent/resin consumption is below 50 kg VOC.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: compliance with the Swiss Waters Protection Ordinance (GSchV), pH 6.5-8.5, no halogenated solvents, no micro-plastic discharge; exhaust air: VOC concentration ≤ 150 mg C/m³ and dry particulate filter capture efficiency ≥ 99%; carbon-fiber dust and epoxy resin waste must be disposed as hazardous/special waste through a BAFU-authorized recycling channel.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cantonal fire safety certificate issued in accordance with VKF/AEAI fire norms; structural load inspection for milling equipment (maximum floor load rating 500 kg/m²); SUVA occupational safety clearance with dated workplace risk assessment and dust exposure monitoring; approved evacuation plan and fire-extinguishing system verified by the local fire brigade.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni ATC); official portal: www.estv.admin.ch; online VAT services and CH-LOGIN are available through the ESTV eService portal. VAT is exclusively federal and is administered by ESTV; corporate income tax is administered federally and by cantonal/communal tax authorities according to the AG's place of effective management and registered seat.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Aktiengesellschaft (AG) in the Swiss Commercial Register (Handelsregister) through the competent cantonal register office. Step 2: Upon registration, the AG automatically receives a permanent Swiss company identifier (UID - Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer / IDE / IDI) in the format CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx, which serves as the general Swiss tax identifier. Step 3: For VAT, submit the registration form to ESTV through the VAT eService portal; ESTV activates the UID with the suffix 'MWST' and issues the final Swiss VAT number in the format CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx MWST. Step 4: A foreign non-resident entity without a Swiss seat or Swiss permanent establishment that makes taxable supplies in Switzerland must appoint a Swiss fiscal/tax representative before registering; the representative files the VAT registration with ESTV, receives the Swiss VAT ID, and assumes joint liability for VAT. Registration is mandatory once Swiss taxable turnover exceeds the statutory threshold and voluntary below it; the registration application should be filed before the taxable activity is continued without VAT compliance. No separate TIN is issued beyond the UID; all tax communications, invoices and customs declarations reference the UID/VAT ID.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss law does not provide a US-style check-the-box election, pass-through election, or elective hybrid classification for an AG. An Aktiengesellschaft is legally and fiscally classified as a resident corporation subject to Swiss corporate income tax at entity level on its worldwide net profits, with double-tax relief and participation relief where applicable. Available elections and administrative mechanisms include: (i) voluntary VAT registration when turnover is below CHF 100,000; (ii) VAT group taxation (Organschaft) for controlled Swiss entities; (iii) the Swiss SME flat-rate VAT method (Saldosteuersatz / taxe forfaitaire) for qualifying businesses; (iv) Swiss tax ruling applications to confirm participation relief, financing structures or export/VAT treatment; and (v) foreign tax credit/relief claims under Swiss double tax treaties. There is no territorial tax election and no tax-exempt-zone regime for an ordinary commercial drone retail AG.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.description_extra_entity_note: The Swiss AG is not pass-through eligible; the entity tax classification is fixed by Swiss corporate law as Entity_Level_Taxation. Income is taxed at the corporate level, and distributed profits are generally subject to Swiss withholding tax when paid to shareholders.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_classification_detail: Resident Swiss AG: taxed at the entity level on net worldwide profits; federal corporate income tax is 8.5% statutory (7.83% effective after deductibility of the federal tax), plus cantonal and communal taxes depending on the AG's seat. The tax_classification_model is Entity_Level_Taxation; no pass-through treatment is allowed. Foreign permanent establishment income may be exempt under Swiss double tax treaties or relieved by credit in non-treaty cases; this does not change the general entity-level classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée / Imposta sul valore aggiunto), governed by the Federal Act on Value Added Tax (SR 641.20) and the Swiss VAT Ordinance (SR 641.201).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 net VAT-exclusive turnover from taxable supplies in Switzerland per business year. Once this threshold is exceeded, VAT registration is mandatory; below it, voluntary registration is available. For foreign-established businesses, the threshold applies with respect to taxable supplies made in Switzerland, and registration requires a Swiss fiscal representative where the foreign supplier has no Swiss seat or permanent establishment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not currently operate a mandatory real-time tax-clearance system, government fiscal API pre-approval, continuous transaction reporting, or digital stamping of invoices. B2B and B2C invoices may be issued on paper or electronically if the recipient can access them and the statutory invoice content is complete. Swiss VAT law requires the invoice to identify the supplier and recipient, describe the supply, state the date, the consideration, the applicable VAT rate and the VAT amount, and show the supplier's Swiss UID/VAT number. Structured electronic invoices such as Swiss eBill, EDI and XML invoices are accepted on a bilateral basis; the Swiss QR-bill is used for payment initiation but is not a fiscal clearance instrument. Taxpayers must preserve all invoices, books and records in machine-readable/auditable form for ESTV inspection; no central government e-invoicing platform is mandatory for commercial retail supplies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: The sale of FPV racing drones, carbon-fiber frames, brushless motors, spare parts and related drone hardware qualifies for Swiss export exemption (0% VAT with input VAT deduction) if the goods are physically removed from the Swiss customs territory and exported to a foreign customer, either directly by the Swiss AG or through a forwarding agent/carrier commissioned by the supplier. The supply to the export vehicle or the final foreign recipient must be supported by proof that the goods left Switzerland. Services: B2B services for foreign-established customers (engineering, firmware/software, assembly support, repair services) are normally regarded as supplied outside Switzerland under the Swiss place-of-supply rules and therefore outside Swiss VAT, with input VAT deduction for the Swiss AG; B2C services are outside Swiss VAT only where the applicable place-of-supply rules so provide. The Swiss AG must document the customer's foreign status, the contract, the delivery/performance chain, and the export event. Input VAT attributable to exports is recoverable through the periodic Swiss VAT return, and resulting input VAT surplus is refunded by ESTV.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration: Swiss customs export declaration, NCTS/e-dec customs transit record, or official electronic export summary evidencing exit of the FPV drones from Swiss customs territory
Transport Document: Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, CMR consignment note, or forwarder's delivery order, signed by the carrier/forwarder and confirming delivery to the foreign customer

Inward Remittance Certificate / Payment Proof: bank statement, SWIFT MT103, PayPal or Stripe settlement report, or inward remittance certificate showing receipt of export proceeds in CHF or foreign currency from the foreign buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ESTV may audit export zero-rating claims, payment-rail settlement reports, customs declarations and delivery records. If export substantiation is missing, incomplete or inconsistent, the export exemption is reversed and the Swiss AG is assessed for output VAT at 8.1% on the sales consideration, together with default interest. Simple VAT evasion is punishable by a fine up to the amount of the tax evaded; aggravated intentional VAT fraud involving forged export documents, phantom deliveries or circular cross-border transactions is punishable by fines up to four times the tax evaded and criminal tax proceedings. The Swiss AG's directors and, for non-established sellers, the Swiss fiscal representative may be jointly and severally liable for unpaid VAT and penalties. Records and export proofs must be retained for at least 10 years; in cases of fraud, ESTV may retrospectively reopen assessments and claw back the VAT advantage beyond the ordinary limitation period, plus interest and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB; German: Schweizerische Nationalbank; French: Banque nationale suisse), Berne and Zurich, is the central monetary and foreign-exchange authority of Switzerland. No separate foreign-exchange control administration exists; the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) regulates banks and financial institutions, and the State Secretariat for International Financial Matters (SIF) coordinates international financial-market policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland provides full de jure and de facto convertibility on both current and capital account under the federal free-movement-of-capital principle and OECD liberalisation commitments. No prior government approval is required for profit remittances, dividend distributions, loan servicing, or capital repatriation by a Swiss AG. The only practical friction is the domestic 35% Swiss withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on dividend and interest payments, which is reducible or eliminated at source under applicable double taxation treaties (0% to 5% for qualifying corporate shareholders, 0% for treaty-eligible interest) upon submission of a tax-domicile certificate (préavis de domicile / Veranlagungsbestätigung). Conversion between CHF, USD, EUR, and offshore CNH occurs at freely market-determined rates; SNB policy interventions, if any, do not constitute convertibility restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Switzerland imposes no statutory surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no prescribed timeline for export receipts generated by ISIC 3240 FPV racing drone sales. A Swiss exporter may retain USD, EUR, CNY/CNH, or other foreign-currency balances indefinitely and select its own conversion schedule. The sole compliance duty is statistical reporting under the SNB balance-of-payments reporting ordinance: direct reporting is required for enterprises whose annual cross-border payments or foreign assets/liabilities exceed approximately CHF 10 million (as periodically revised), and individual export transactions may be sampled below that threshold. Failure to report is an administrative offence under the Swiss National Bank Act but does not restrict the exporter's free use of proceeds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Sperrkonto) for the CHF 100,000 AG minimum capital; multi-currency Operational Account (CHF/USD/EUR/CNH) with SIC, SEPA, SWIFT, and e-FX dealing platform
Capital Escrow Account (Sperrkonto) plus Operational Account with cantonal guarantee, trade finance desk, and FX execution portal
Operational Account with merchant acquiring support and trade finance; capital escrow account available on request
Operational Account in CHF/EUR/USD with SIC and e-bill rails; no standalone capital-escrow confirmation service for AG incorporation

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM as a complementary collection rail for PayPal/Stripe marketplace payouts, but LOW as a substitute for a Swiss bank account. Legal constraints: offshore digital EMIs (Revolut Business, Wise Business, Airwallex, Payoneer) typically hold foreign e-money licences (FCA, PSD2), not a FINMA banking licence. They cannot provide SIC settlement access, cannot issue the bank confirmation required for AG share-capital deposit, and are not protected by the Swiss esisuisse deposit guarantee. CHF balances at EMIs are held through partner banks and are not treated as regulated deposits. EMIs may be used to collect low-ticket e-commerce receivables, provided their AML/KYC framework satisfies Swiss expectations, but statutory capital, corporate taxes, consolidated liquidity, and core treasury balances must reside at a FINMA-regulated bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Swiss AG with non-resident shareholders or foreign-resident directors, the default mandate requires at least one director with individual signature authority (signature individuelle) to appear physically at a Swiss bank branch for the onboarding interview, presenting original passport, apostilled corporate documents, and the current commercial-registry extract. Pure remote or video onboarding is accepted only for low-risk Swiss-resident UBOs and generally does not extend to opening the blocked capital-escrow account. In the incorporation phase, the founders and the designated chairperson must personally sign the bank forms before an authorised bank officer; e-banking tokens or SwissID acceleration do not replace the in-person mandate for non-resident ownership structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owners or signatories from a FATF/FINMA watch-listed jurisdiction, or a US person/passport appearing in the ownership or signature chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificate of incorporation, notarised and apostilled articles of association (Statuten), current Handelsregisterauszug, official UBO declaration, source-of-wealth documentation for each beneficial owner above 10%, negative-media and sanctions-screening report, Swiss tax-residence certificates for all UBOs, and a board resolution defining the corporate treasury purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dual-use concern: FPV racing drones (carbon-fibre frames, brushless motors, video transmitters) flagged by bank sanctions or export-control screening as potential UAV or defence-adjacent goods
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Technical data sheets evidencing sub-250g racing class and non-weaponised configuration; SECO free-export statement (Unbedenklichkeitsbescheinigung) or General Export Certificate confirming non-dual-use classification; end-user and end-use declarations from retail distributors; component specifications (ESC, camera, motors) proving hobby-grade design; and an external legal opinion confirming no strategic-goods licence is required under Swiss/EU dual-use rules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Abnormal cross-border wire pattern: foreign capital injection followed by rapid outbound payments to electronics suppliers in Shenzhen or Hong Kong before revenue or production is evidenced
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised capital-allotment resolution; SWIFT MT103 vouchers with exact remittance information ('Aktienkapital-Einzahlung'); executed purchase contracts and pro-forma invoices from component vendors; customs declarations and transport documents (AWB/CMR); inventory evidence; and audited cash-flow projections demonstrating commercial justification for the international payment flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-ticket e-commerce settlement through PayPal and Stripe showing elevated refund rates, chargeback ratios, or cross-border marketplace selling patterns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PCI-DSS certification for the online store; platform merchant-ID and settlement statements; formal refund-and-return policy; chargeback-dispute management workflow; Swiss VAT (MWST) registration certificate and VAT returns; historical transaction categorisation reports; and a low-risk AML rating memo for ISIC 3240 retail FPV drones as approved by the bank's risk matrix.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The AG's initial share capital (minimum CHF 100,000, with at least CHF 50,000 paid up) must be transferred by shareholders to the blocked capital-escrow account (Sperrkonto) at a Swiss bank via SWIFT MT103. The beneficiary field must identify the company and state 'Aktienkapital - Sperrkonto'; the remittance information must read 'Einlage auf das Aktienkapital'. The incorporation auditor obtains the bank's written confirmation of deposit (Einzahlungsbestätigung). For foreign shareholders, the transaction is recorded under the SNB balance-of-payments direct-investment equity-capital category; no SNB or FINMA approval is required. Verification checklist: (i) board resolution allotting shares; (ii) UBO disclosure; (iii) bank escrow confirmation; (iv) notarised filing of the articles. Distribution or repayment of capital before registration, or in breach of Article 680 of the Swiss Code of Obligations (restriction on repayment of paid-in capital), is prohibited.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: (1) Swiss domestic CHF disbursements via the SIC payment system with immediate finality; (2) EUR payments via SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant (SCT Inst) for routine suppliers and SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA counterparts; (3) USD and CNH payments via SWIFT MT103/MT202 (settled through CHIPS or correspondent banking networks); for RMB-denominated procurement, conversion through a Swiss trade-finance desk or use of an offshore CNH account; (4) high-value batch procurement of brushless motors, carbon-fibre frames, and electronics under confirmed irrevocable commercial letters of credit issued via SWIFT MT700 under UCP 600, with inspection certificates and transport documents; (5) retail refunds and e-commerce payouts settled through PayPal/Stripe balances and SEPA direct debits. Treasury policy: maintain committed intraday headroom in CHF/EUR/USD at the primary bank, execute daily sweeps from marketplace settlement accounts, and require dual-authorisation (double signature) for any transfer exceeding CHF 50,000 equivalent.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (CHF/USD, CHF/EUR, CHF/CNH) up to 12 months against committed trade flows, booked under a Swiss bank ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with credit support annex
FX swaps (swap-in/swap-out) for rolling short-term liquidity in USD/EUR/CNH executed via the bank's e-FX dealing platform
Cross-currency swaps (USD/CHF, EUR/CHF) to hedge long-term supplier-financing obligations or foreign-currency treasury positions
Offshore USD/CNH non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) to hedge RMB procurement costs from Chinese component vendors where onshore CNY market access is unavailable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax and capital tax return, including certified annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal and communal tax administration (Steuerverwaltung); federal corporate income tax assessed by the canton on behalf of the Federal Tax Administration (ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally 15 June following the accounting year-end; extension to 30 September obtainable upon application; for calendar year 2025, due 15 June 2026
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest up to 3.0% per annum plus penal interest under cantonal tax law; late filing warnings and summary criminal prosecution in cases of willful evasion; persistent non-filing combined with organizational deficiency may trigger court-ordered administrative strike-off from the commercial register under OR Art. 731b/c

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Swiss VAT settlement return (VAT return filed via ESTV electronic portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung - ESTV), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For annually settled VAT payers, no later than 30 April after the corresponding VAT period; quarterly interim payments made as determined in VAT assessment notice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fine up to CHF 5,000 plus default interest of current statutory VAT default rate; continued omission may lead to criminal procedure under VAT Act with additional penalty up to CHF 10,000; not directly connected to commercial register strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual wage declaration to old-age and survivors' insurance (AHV/ALV/NBU), including salary certificates and social insurance totals
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse) responsible for the registered office of the employer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 30 April of the calendar year following the wage year; for wage year 2025, due 30 April 2026
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative surcharge of up to 5% of outstanding contributions, default interest, and fines for intentionally incorrect or omitted statements; insolvency notification may be initiated in cases of non-payment; no direct commercial register effect

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting minutes, shareholder resolutions, and profit appropriation documentation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate statutory records at registered office; no deposit with the Swiss Commercial Register unless capital changes or board changes require formal registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: General meeting must be held within six months after the balance sheet date; minutes finalised and filed with minutes book on the same day
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Shareholder right to challenge resolutions under OR Art. 706; board liability for delayed or inadequate convening; administrative find and possible commercial register observations; if the company lacks a legal board and loses registered address, the commercial registry authority may initiate strike-off under OR Art. 731b/c

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary independent audit is compulsory if the company exceeds, in two consecutive business years, any two of the following three thresholds: total assets CHF 20 million, net revenue CHF 40 million, and average annual workforce of 250 employees. A limited audit remains required for companies not opting out unless all shareholders validly consent to opt out of audit in writing; opt-out is only available for companies not exceeding 10 full-time employees and not meeting audit requirements under special law. If a shareholder holding 10% of voting rights requests an audit in writing, appointment of an auditor is mandatory.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR Art. 957-963) financial reporting framework; local accounting in French, German or Italian; annual financial statements prepared under Swiss GAAP (Swiss GAAP FER) if statutory audit is performed under ordinary rules or if voluntarily adopted; IFRS permitted as a substitute framework and mandatory for listed or regulated financial companies; simplified bookkeeping may apply for sole proprietorships but not for AG.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss law imposes an obligation to maintain and update an internal register of beneficial owners (beherrschende Personen) and of any shareholders exceeding 25% of voting rights or exercising effective control. There is no public annual confirmation filing to the commercial register; however, the board of directors must, at least annually and on every transfer of shares, verify the shareholders' declarations and update the register. The statutory auditor reviews the completeness of the register during the annual audit. Instruction from the shareholder to transfer shares is executed only after the beneficial owner declaration is received and processed.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Signatories (Verzeichnis des Verwaltungsrates)
Minute Book and shareholder resolution records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 350 - 1,000 USD per annum (typical CHF 300-800) depending on canton and provider; includes registered office address, mail forwarding and Commercial Register change coordination
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Limited audit: 4,500 - 13,500 USD; ordinary statutory audit: 17,000 - 45,000 USD depending on size, volume of transactions and IFRS/Swiss GAAP FER applicability

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% Swiss federal corporate income tax on after-tax net profit (effective 7.83% on pre-tax profit); combined federal plus cantonal and municipal rates range from approx. 11.9% (Obwalden) and 14.6% (Zug) to approx. 21.1% (Zurich City), depending on tax jurisdiction of the registered seat.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Patent box regime exempting up to 90% of qualifying self-developed IP income; incremental R&D super-deduction of 50% of qualifying R&D costs (capped at 80% of attributable R&D payroll); notional interest deduction (NID) on additional equity in cantons that adopted the optional rule (e.g. Zurich); participation relief for qualifying dividends and capital gains; combined effective rate for a typical manufacturing/trading AG in Zug approximately 14.6%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined federal and cantonal corporate income tax return for legal entities (ESTV form 'Steuererklaerung juristische Personen' / federal form K accompanied by the cantonal schedule, e.g. Zug 'EASY', Zurich 'KM 11'); electronic filing through the 'eTax' platform of the Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) and the relevant canton's e-portal; two intrastate instalments (federal and cantonal) are assessed in one administrative procedure.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filed within six months after the end of the business year (art. 125/126 DBG and cantonal practice); calendar-year AGs generally receive a filing deadline of 30 June of the following year; extensions of up to six months are available on justified written application; tax returns filed late accrue interest from the original due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory net profit or loss before income tax per the audited profit and loss statement in CHF.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not file this return; the AG reports its worldwide Swiss-attributable profit; branch profits of a Swiss permanent establishment are pooled into Box 1.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Equity capital base used for the cantonal/municipal capital tax (Zug 0.07%; Zurich approx. 0.13%).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Equity is taxable at entity level irrespective of the residence of shareholders; participation shareholdings of 10% or more may be deducted where eligible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualifying dividends and capital gains from qualifying holdings of at least 10% of the share capital or with a market value exceeding CHF 1 million are exempt from federal and cantonal income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Applies to the Swiss-resident AG only; foreign investors claiming treaty benefits on the distribution must apply separately through the WHT refund mechanism.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualifying net income from Swiss or foreign registered patents, utility and similar IP rights is eligible for up to 90% exemption.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Relief requires genuine Swiss R&D substance and registered IP owned and exploited by the Swiss AG; the box does not apply to foreign bare licensors.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible losses from prior years carried forward for seven consecutive assessment periods.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses sustained by the same Swiss legal entity and pre-acquisition losses subject to the change-of-control restriction (art. 67 DBG) are deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final reconciled taxable base after all reliefs; federal CIT at 8.5% on after-tax profit and cantonal/municipal rates applied here.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The returned taxable profit must be reconcilable with the audited financial statements; any unexplained variance triggers audit inquiries.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers written reminders with reminder fees, procedural fines (Ordnungsbusse) of up to CHF 1,000 per canton, and late payment interest of 4.5% to 6% p.a.; wilful failure to file constitutes a procedural offence under art. 174 DBG with fines up to CHF 10,000; for tax evasion, the penalty equals the evaded tax plus a surcharge of 25% to 50% (federal) and up to 200% (cantonal).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on all dividends and profit distributions paid by the AG, regardless of beneficiary residence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Treaty relief is granted through ESTV Form 823 or through the advance relief procedure (V-RTS / EESA), under which the paying bank or the AG may apply a reduced rate upon prior approval of the ESTV; the claimant must submit a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) from the foreign competent authority together with Form 823, and must satisfy the six-month minimum holding period and the economic substance/anti-abuse conditions; refund applications must be filed inside three years from the end of the calendar year in which the dividend became due; DTA rates typically range from 0% (wholly-owned subsidiaries) to 15% (portfolio) depending on the counterparty treaty, e.g. 5% under the US-Swiss DTA for qualified shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: Switzerland imposes no domestic withholding tax on outbound IP royalties (statutory rate 0%); most Swiss DTAs provide 0% or a reduced 5% royalty rate. Interest: the 35% withholding tax applies only to interest on issued bonds, bank deposits and structured money-market instruments under the Verrechnungssteuergesetz; ordinary intercompany trade credit and interest on standard bank loans payable to non-banks are not subject to WHT; treaty rates are often 0% for financial institutions and 10% under older DTAs, subject to the beneficiary declaration and arm's-length conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full Swiss Master File and Local File documentation is required where the multinational group reaches consolidated gross revenue of CHF 50 million; simplified contemporaneous documentation applies to intra-group transactions of CHF 10 million or more; Country-by-Country Reporting applies to groups with consolidated revenue of CHF 900 million or more with mandatory filing via the ESTV.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not operate an OECD-style ESR register, but economic substance is enforced through (i) the global minimum tax (Pillar Two) effective 1 January 2024, applying a 15% top-up tax to groups with annual revenue of EUR 750 million or more; (ii) the BEPS Multilateral Instrument and treaty-benefit anti-abuse clauses requiring real business activity for DTA relief; and (iii) settled case law requiring permanent establishment, qualified staffing, premises and actual decision-taking in Switzerland for participation relief and WHT refunds; an AG holding only passive rights or using nominee directors without local operations risks denial of treaty benefits, administrative assistance to the foreign tax administration and reclassification of profits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully or negligently under-declaring taxable profit, inflating deductions or omitting drone retail sales through an unregistered foreign distribution vehicle.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Restitution of the evaded federal tax plus a fine of 25% to 50% of the evaded amount; cantonal fines up to 200% of the evaded tax; the assessment may be reopened for ten years (objective Nachsteuer); criminal interest accrues at 5% p.a.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed or authorised the false declaration are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax with their personal assets under art. 759 CO; criminal convictions trigger personal fines and exclusion from board positions; pre-trial travel bans and asset freezes are routinely ordered.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting falsified, forged or materially incorrect business books or invoices, e.g. fabricated supplier invoices for carbon-fibre milling services or fictitious payroll records for contract assemblers connected to a Chinese affiliate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of up to five years (art. 186 DBG) in addition to restitution of the evaded tax and accrued interest; the criminal court may order forfeiture of the proceeds of crime; administrative assessments are reopened without time limit in connection with the criminal act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The acting director or CFO is prosecuted personally; the company is jointly liable for fines under art. 177 DBG for offences committed in the course of business; travel bans, confiscation orders and disqualification from serving as directors apply to the natural persons involved.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends, capital reductions or disguised profit transfers to non-resident shareholders without assessing and remitting the 35% Verrechnungssteuer, or routing funds through artificial hybrid securities to avoid the withholding layer.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unpaid withholding tax is collected from the AG together with interest at 5% p.a.; a penalty of up to 100% of the undeclared WHT is imposed; deliberate concealment may double the administrative fine; the claim provokes liquidation and bankruptcy proceedings if unpaid.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the withholding tax if the distribution is made after they know or should have known that the tax was not declared; criminal liability for the responsible officer carries up to three years imprisonment; the board is disqualified from executing further distributions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Controlled transactions at non-arm's-length prices, e.g. purchasing FPV drone components from a Chinese related party at a 70% markup, or paying excessive licence fees to an IP-holding entity in a preferential jurisdiction, thereby shifting Swiss profit abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation and adjustment of taxable profit under art. 58 DBG as a constructive dividend, triggering the 35% withholding tax unless a DTA limits the rate; interest and penalties on the adjustment; Pillar Two top-up tax at 15% applies to in-scope groups; a concealed adjustment may be prosecuted as tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members approving or signing defective transfer pricing documentation face personal liability for the adjusted tax under art. 759 CO; falsification of financial statements (art. 163 CO) carries imprisonment of up to three years; travel bans and disgorgement against the directors personally follow the criminal judgement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML shell-company abuse and money laundering
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the AG as a shell with no real substance, uncontrolled nominee directors, or processing retail payments through PayPal and Stripe without proper AML verification and compliance with the Anti-Money Laundering Act (GwG) in order to launder illicit proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering under art. 260bis StGB is punishable by imprisonment of up to three years and a fine; aggravated cases impose longer sentences; FINMA may impose administrative enforcement measures, license withdrawals and publish sanction decisions; failure to report suspicious transactions to the Money Laundering Reporting Office (MROS) triggers administrative fines and automatic dissolution procedures; Swiss/EU sanction violations run in parallel.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the compliance officer are prosecuted as natural persons under the CDB 20 rules with personal fines up to CHF 500,000; nominee directors are individually incriminated under art. 260bis StGB independent of the company; the court may order travel bans, asset freezes, personal restitution orders and a de facto insolvency of the entity, with the board disqualified from managing any company for up to five years.
